verdict.rationale: Appwrite Functions provide first-party background automation. They can be triggered by server events and scheduled executions, run as cron jobs and event handlers in isolated runtimes, and the docs also mention scheduled messaging. However, the evidence covers only developer-written trigger and cron code, not AI-native or agent-driven autonomous automations, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration. missing for 10: AI- or agent-driven autonomous automation (as opposed to hand-coded cron and event functions), documentation of background run management and monitoring, independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: These Functions can be triggered by HTTP requests, SDK methods, server events, webhooks, and scheduled executions.
Run API endpoints, webhooks, cron jobs, and event handlers in secure isolated runtimes that scale with demand.
Send and schedule email, SMS, and push notifications.
